Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10032 at 14 FR 429 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed January 28, 1949; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the February 1, 1949 issue. Inventory: one whole-order clause, the dossier span at offsets 580 to 2224 of the held text, from the order's heading through its last operative sentence (the sentence barring changes in conditions). Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Akron, Canton & Youngstown Railroad Company and certain other carriers designated in a list attached to the order, and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars any of the carriers involved or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. The list of carriers (Eastern, Western and Southeastern regions) follows the signature block in the held text; it identifies the carriers and is not a separate command.
